column1: # THE CORRESPONDENCE, WRITTEN DOWN ONCE.  Two trees carry the same object
# language, and what tied them was a tag string one side matched and the other
# happened to emit — so a former only one tree had did not fail, it was simply
# never generated, and every sweep over the bridge reported green about shapes
# it was never handed.  This file is the one declaration of the pairing, and
# `scripts/check-formers.py` holds four surfaces to it: the Agda datatype, the
# Agda decoder, the TypeScript union and the TypeScript generator.
# A NEW FORMER IS THEREFORE SIX EDITS, AND THAT IS THE POINT — the fifth is
# this line, and until it exists the other four are each separately red.  The
# GEN=no DECLARES A FORMER THE GENERATOR CANNOT REACH, and it is a finding
# parked rather than an exemption granted: a former nothing generates is a
# former no sweep and no oracle run has ever covered, whatever either reports.
# It is written here rather than in the generator so that the hole is counted
# where the pairing is read, and the reason is the last column.
# ROLE IS THE DIVIDING TEST'S VERDICT, AND EVERY `exp` ROW OWES ONE.  The test
# is whether an operator SUBSCRIBES anything or reads the protocol's own
# bookkeeping; what it decides is which formers the one pure-function former
# absorbs.  That verdict used to live in memory and in one header's prose, so
# a former's status was answerable only by whoever had last thought about it
# — and a former added later inherited no obligation to have a status at all.
# The vocabulary is closed, so a new answer is a change to the checker and
#   source    produces without reading anything, and subscribes nothing
#   pure      a pure function of ONE value, with or without carried state
#   protocol  reads or writes the protocol's own bookkeeping
#   flatten   subscribes a payload that is literal syntax and must be RUN
#   binder    not an operator at all — μ-binding structure
#   -         the value language and the primitive operators, neither of
#             which is a stream former, so the test does not apply
# The reasoning behind each verdict is NOT here: it is in the header of the
# one pure-function former, which is where the test is stated, and a second
# copy of it would be the copy that ages.
